exceptions: T/B receptor cues are greatly enlarged schematic symbols.
Granules are enlarged reduced representative samples.

functional_sequences.title: Biconcavity and oxygen carriage
functional_sequences.mechanism: Hemoglobin carries oxygen between lungs and tissues; the retained section explains the cell shape.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Read the cell surface
steps.explanation: Match the smooth whole discs to the dumbbell section. The biconcave body offers a large exchange surface and a thin central region. Mature mammalian red cells lack a nucleus.
steps.unmodeled_context: Hemoglobin, membrane proteins and cytoskeleton are not separate parts.

steps.title: Load oxygen in the lung
steps.explanation: In pulmonary exchange, oxygen enters the red cell and binds hemoglobin. Explain this with the retained cell, without changing its color to claim an oxygenation measurement.
steps.unmodeled_context: No alveolus, capillary, oxygen gradient or binding kinetics are modeled.

steps.title: Deliver oxygen to tissue
steps.explanation: Oxygen can dissociate for tissue delivery. The section shows a short path through the thin center, while the flexible cell membrane permits passage through narrow vessels.
steps.unmodeled_context: No deformation, vascular transit or measured diffusion is simulated.

structure_function_links: The section links whole-cell biconcavity to exchange surface and thin center.
Anucleate appearance identifies the mature erythrocyte, not a nucleus hidden by clipping.

questions.prompt: Does central pallor mean the center is a hole?
questions.answer: No. The retained cross-section shows a thin continuous center.

questions.prompt: Can this view give oxygen saturation?
questions.answer: No. It is a structural comparison without an oxygenation field.

schematic_limitations: True cell scale is retained; camera magnification does not enlarge physical cells.
The sample of three whole cells does not represent a blood count.

functional_sequences.title: Rouleau as an aggregation pattern
functional_sequences.mechanism: Contrast stacked red cells with isolated discs and with a platelet-fibrin clot.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Compare face-to-face stacking
steps.explanation: The retained seven-cell stack illustrates rouleau morphology. Each disc retains its red-cell identity and dimensions.
steps.unmodeled_context: No dynamic aggregation or sedimentation exists; plasma-protein electrostatics are outside the geometry.

steps.title: Distinguish the clot corner
steps.explanation: Compare this separately authored platelet-fibrin example with the red-cell stack. A rouleau stack is not a fibrin strand or a platelet plug.
steps.unmodeled_context: The two scenes are illustrative examples, not stages of one computed trajectory.

structure_function_links: Disc surfaces support a face-to-face stacking comparison; clot fibers and platelet protrusions have different identities.

questions.prompt: Does the seven-cell stack establish a diagnosis or an ESR value?
questions.answer: No. It displays morphology only; a clinical smear and laboratory measurement are separate.

schematic_limitations: Do not animate red cells into fibrin or infer a protein concentration from the chosen arrangement.

functional_sequences.title: Neutrophil maturation and intracellular killing
functional_sequences.mechanism: Compare nuclear maturation, then explain compartmentalized microbial killing.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Compare mature and band carriers
steps.explanation: The mature sample has four linked lobes; the band sample has a continuous curved nucleus. Both nuclei and both granule samples are selected together through the shared named parts.
steps.unmodeled_context: Shared parts prevent independently selecting the two nuclear/granule carriers. Segmentation is a maturation comparison, not a simulated aging clock.

steps.title: Engulf a microorganism
steps.explanation: A neutrophil encloses an ingested microbe in a phagosome. Stored granules fuse with this compartment and deliver antimicrobial contents.
steps.unmodeled_context: The phagosome, microbe, membranes and fusion events are narrative context; retained granules do not move or disappear.

steps.title: Combine enzymes and oxidants
steps.explanation: NADPH oxidase generates oxidants at the phagosome; granule MPO uses hydrogen peroxide and chloride to generate hypochlorous acid. Granule proteins and oxidants cooperate in killing.
steps.unmodeled_context: Oxidase, MPO and chemical species are not individually modeled. Granule colors do not encode specific enzyme content or classes.

structure_function_links: A lobulated nucleus is a morphological marker of maturity.
Cytoplasmic granules provide stored antimicrobial material; their location supports the distinction from nuclear chromatin.

questions.prompt: Why does selecting Neutrophil nucleus also show the band nucleus?
questions.answer: The source combines both carriers in that one named part.

questions.prompt: Do neutrophil granules attack only by release outside the cell?
questions.answer: No. Fusion into the phagosome is a principal route for intracellular killing.

schematic_limitations: Nucleus-only isolation can be misleading; always retain both carrier cells for maturation.
Granules are enlarged representative samples, not a natural census.
Recruitment, rolling, diapedesis and chemotaxis require unmodeled endothelium/tissue.

functional_sequences.title: Eosinophil granules and extracellular targets
functional_sequences.mechanism: Recruitment and activation can release cytotoxic products used in parasite defense and allergic tissue injury.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Find the distinctive granules
steps.explanation: Pair the bilobed nucleus with the large orange granules in cytoplasm. Their bright color is a stain cue rather than an activity measurement.
steps.unmodeled_context: The selected sample is a schematic section with reduced granule counts.

steps.title: Explain recruitment and release
steps.explanation: At inflammatory tissue sites, activated eosinophils can release MBP, ECP, EDN and eosinophil peroxidase. These can act on extracellular parasites and also injure host tissue in allergy.
steps.unmodeled_context: The target parasite, epithelium, activating receptors and release route are not modeled.

steps.title: Separate two protein identities
steps.explanation: The major-basic-protein granule core and galectin-10 Charcot-Leyden crystals are distinct. Use the corrected description; this model does not contain a Charcot-Leyden crystal part.
steps.unmodeled_context: The galectin-10 result comes from the anatomy specialist opened primary source, not crystal geometry here.

structure_function_links: Large cytoplasmic granules store effector proteins; the nucleus remains a separate compartment.

questions.prompt: Is a Charcot-Leyden crystal the crystallized MBP granule core?
questions.answer: No. It is composed of galectin-10; use anatomy correction eos_gran.
No. It is the retained histology teaching color.

schematic_limitations: Do not depict every helminth as phagocytosed.
No secretion timing or tissue-damage dose is encoded.

functional_sequences.title: Basophil granules and IgE-triggered release
functional_sequences.mechanism: Receptor-bound IgE crosslinking is one activation route leading to granule release.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Locate nucleus and cytoplasmic granules
steps.explanation: Coarse dark granules can obscure the nucleus in a smear projection. The section separates their cytoplasmic location from the nuclear interior.
steps.unmodeled_context: Do not move granules into the nucleus to mimic a two-dimensional smear.

steps.title: Explain the IgE receptor trigger
steps.explanation: An allergen can crosslink IgE already bound to Fc-epsilon-RI and activate the basophil. Other inflammatory stimuli can activate it too.
steps.unmodeled_context: IgE, allergen and Fc-epsilon-RI are not modeled; do not reuse the B-cell surface-Ig cue for basophil IgE.

steps.title: Distinguish stored and newly generated mediators
steps.explanation: Activated basophils release stored histamine from granules and can generate leukotriene C4 and cytokines. These products participate in immune and allergic responses.
steps.unmodeled_context: Granules remain static; histamine, LTC4 and cytokines have no geometry or simulated concentration.

structure_function_links: Visible cytoplasmic granules are a storage compartment; a visible S/bilobed nucleus remains separate.

questions.prompt: Is a basophil just a circulating mast cell?
questions.answer: No. They share some mechanisms but are distinct cell types.

questions.prompt: Is every released mediator a stored granule constituent?
questions.answer: No. Newly generated lipid mediators and cytokines must be distinguished from stored histamine.

schematic_limitations: This sequence does not quantify mediator release or anaphylaxis.

functional_sequences.title: Same resting morphology, different recognition
functional_sequences.mechanism: Use retained receptor symbols to explain conventional T-cell and B-cell recognition, then distinguish resting cells from effector differentiation.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Compare the small cells
steps.explanation: Both small resting samples retain the same cell size and ordinary smear morphology. Their nuclei dominate the cell and leave a thin cytoplasmic rim.
steps.unmodeled_context: T/B identity cannot be inferred from this retained morphology; enlarged receptor symbols are functional annotations.

steps.title: Read the paired T-receptor cue
steps.explanation: The conventional alpha-beta TCR recognizes peptide together with its MHC carrier on another cell. Peptide-MHC recognition is required context; an unattached native antigen is not the depicted TCR ligand.
steps.unmodeled_context: No MHC, peptide, presenting cell, CD3, CD4/CD8 or co-stimulatory molecules are present. The model does not represent every T-cell subset.

steps.title: Read membrane-bound surface Ig
steps.explanation: B-cell surface immunoglobulin can bind intact/native antigen directly. The gold Y remains a membrane receptor on the resting B cell, not a secreted antibody.
steps.unmodeled_context: Antigen binding and receptor signaling are narrative context; cue dimensions are greatly enlarged.

steps.title: Describe later outcomes
steps.explanation: After appropriate activation, helper T cells coordinate responses and cytotoxic T cells kill target cells. B cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasmablasts/plasma cells and memory cells.
steps.unmodeled_context: No T-cell subset, activation state, plasma cell, target killing or antibody secretion is modeled. Resting B remains nonsecreting.

steps.title: Check what size can tell you
steps.explanation: The retained large sample provides a size and nuclear-to-cytoplasmic comparison. Size alone does not identify activation or natural-killer identity.
steps.unmodeled_context: No separate large-lymphocyte cytotoxic granules exist; do not claim they can be selected.

structure_function_links: The cues are attached functional symbols while cell morphology remains comparable.
The broader cytoplasmic rim of the large sample supports comparison without establishing a lineage or activation state.

questions.answer: Conventional TCR: peptide-MHC; B-cell surface Ig: intact/native antigen.

questions.prompt: Does the gold Y leave this resting B cell as antibody?
questions.answer: No. Secretion belongs to subsequent plasmablast/plasma-cell differentiation.

questions.prompt: Can these colors distinguish resting T and B cells on a clinical smear?
questions.answer: No. Functional symbols and authored colors are teaching annotations.

schematic_limitations: Do not use the native Playback control as proof of activation; blood_cells has no animation sidecar.
Cue shape is not a molecular reconstruction and cannot be measured as receptor size.
The conventional alpha-beta example does not include gamma-delta, MAIT or iNKT recognition systems.

functional_sequences.title: Blood monocyte and recruited tissue effector
functional_sequences.mechanism: Explain monocyte recruitment and possible differentiation without making adult monocytes the universal origin of resident macrophages.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Read the monocyte section
steps.explanation: Identify the large cell and kidney/notched nuclear profile in the comparison row. Cytoplasm and nucleus are distinct selectable parts.
steps.unmodeled_context: Morphology does not identify a monocyte subset or a tissue macrophage.

steps.title: Explain tissue recruitment
steps.explanation: A recruited circulating monocyte can enter tissue and differentiate into a macrophage. This is a possible pathway rather than the origin of every resident macrophage population.
steps.unmodeled_context: Endothelium, recruitment ligands and differentiated tissue cell are unmodeled.

steps.title: Connect to tissue function
steps.explanation: Macrophages can engulf and destroy microbes and debris, release cytokines, and present antigen to T cells. These later functions require tissue context beyond this blood-cell specimen.
steps.unmodeled_context: No phagosome, antigen-presenting complex, tissue resident cell or differentiation motion is included.

structure_function_links: The monocyte body illustrates a cell available for recruitment; its notched nucleus is a morphology cue, not a migration mechanism.

questions.prompt: Does this imply that adult circulating monocytes routinely become microglia?
questions.answer: No. Apply anatomy correction mono: microglia are principally embryonically derived.

questions.prompt: Can this model display a macrophage phagosome?
questions.answer: No. That mechanism is described beside the retained blood monocyte.

schematic_limitations: Lineage conclusions are limited by anatomy specialist primary evidence; no human lineage percentage is claimed.

functional_sequences.title: Platelet activation, aggregation and fibrin reinforcement
functional_sequences.mechanism: Contrast resting and activated shapes, separate mediator sources, then explain clot stabilization.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Inspect resting discs
steps.explanation: The four retained platelet fragments illustrate the resting disc shape. They are anucleate and much smaller than the leukocyte samples.
steps.unmodeled_context: Four examples are not a platelet count or an activation assay.

steps.title: Explain adhesion at injury
steps.explanation: At vessel injury, VWF connects exposed collagen to platelet GPIb/IX. Activation produces protrusions and changes the platelet surface for aggregation.
steps.unmodeled_context: No damaged wall, collagen, VWF or receptor geometry exists; the Clot view shows two separate activated examples.

steps.title: Separate release from synthesis
steps.explanation: Dense granules release stored ADP and serotonin; alpha granules release proteins such as VWF. Separately, membrane arachidonic acid is converted through COX and PGH2 to TxA2 by thromboxane synthase. TxA2 helps amplify activation.
steps.unmodeled_context: There are no selectable platelet granule classes or mediator particles. TxA2 must never be described as stored granule cargo.

steps.title: Describe fibrinogen bridges
steps.explanation: Activated alpha-IIb-beta-3 (GPIIb/IIIa) binds fibrinogen, bridging neighboring platelets into an aggregate. This platelet plug is reinforced by coagulation.
steps.unmodeled_context: No individual integrin or soluble fibrinogen is modeled; existing Fibrin is not the fibrinogen bridge.

steps.title: Inspect the fibrin network
steps.explanation: Platelet surfaces support coagulation complexes; thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into fibrin. Polymerization and factor-XIII crosslinking strengthen the plug. The retained ten fiber paths meet the activated platelet exteriors.
steps.unmodeled_context: Ten paths are illustrative; geometry is not a coagulation-rate, crosslink count or clot-strength result.

steps.title: Explain later fibrinolysis
steps.explanation: During repair, plasmin generated from plasminogen can cleave fibrin. Explain removal beside the retained mesh; do not hide fibers as evidence of simulated dissolution.
steps.unmodeled_context: No plasmin, plasminogen, tissue repair or dynamic fibrinolysis is modeled.

structure_function_links: Resting discs and activated protrusions show a structural state contrast.
Fibrin exterior contacts provide a teaching cue for reinforcement, while excluding fibers through opaque platelet interiors.

questions.prompt: Which is synthesized rather than released from storage granules: ADP, serotonin or TxA2?
questions.answer: TxA2 is synthesized from arachidonic acid; ADP and serotonin are stored dense-granule contents.

questions.prompt: Are the visible fibers fibrinogen bridges?
questions.answer: No. Fibrinogen bridges bind platelet integrins; modeled Fibrin represents the polymerized reinforcement.

questions.prompt: Does selecting Clot animate the resting platelets?
questions.answer: No. It changes camera and visibility to two separate retained activated examples.

schematic_limitations: Adhesion, secretion, aggregation and coagulation overlap biologically; the ordered explanation is not a kinetic timeline.
Do not invent flow, molecular binding, contraction or drug-dose controls.
Clot retraction is not simulated; no new motion requested.

functional_sequences.title: Plasma carries dissolved components
functional_sequences.mechanism: Relate the fluid domain to formed elements without treating its box volume as hematocrit.
functional_sequences.presentation: ordered narrative using existing static geometry and native view/selection/framing

steps.title: Enable optional context
steps.explanation: The translucent domain denotes the liquid surrounding cells. Plasma transports dissolved nutrients, proteins and other substances.
steps.unmodeled_context: The rectangular boundary is a viewing context rather than a natural vessel wall.

steps.title: Return to structure comparison
steps.explanation: Return to Comparison to read the formed elements clearly. Hidden plasma is a display choice, not removal of extracellular fluid from blood.
steps.unmodeled_context: Cell number and domain volume are illustrative; neither gives a blood differential or hematocrit.

structure_function_links: Transparent optional plasma avoids obscuring structures and places their transport context around them.

questions.prompt: Does the translucent box establish a physiological plasma percentage?
questions.answer: No. Its bounds and transparency are authored display context.

schematic_limitations: Transparency is not concentration, viscosity or flow velocity.
